paragraphs: I code with Codex and Claude Code: I set rules in AGENTS.md, work in milestones and review diffs and tests. I published Premium Frontend Director, an open-source skill for coding agents.

featured.description: Website for Aitana Mora González’s culinary project, with tasting menus, online reservations and a dashboard for the restaurant team.

One place for a photo or video studio's workflow, from quotes and session planning to invoices and delivery through a private gallery. Includes an assistant that drafts session plans and recommends gear with an in-browser language model (WebLLM/WebGPU), with Ollama as an option.
evidence: Problem — Studio work is scattered across calendars, spreadsheets and galleries.
Technical decision — The React demo uses local fictional data and lets visitors explore the workflow without saving changes.
Verification — Tests cover the calendar, client details and gallery favourites. The Codex guide defines acceptance criteria and change review.
featured.imageAlt: LumaFlow Studio demo dashboard with fictional sessions, clients, invoices and deliveries.

featured.description: My photography archive, arranged into series you can filter and browse one image at a time. I generate the pages statically with Next.js.

other.title: Distrito Gourmet
other.description: Customers can browse the menu, place an order and book a table. Staff run the restaurant through separate dashboards for the dining room, kitchen and administration.
other.imageAlt: Distrito Gourmet home page with a photo of grilled octopus and links to the menu and reservations.
evidence: Problem — Menus, reservations and orders are often managed in separate tools.
Technical decision — The React interface uses a Laravel API with permissions for customers, staff and administrators.
Verification — Tests cover availability, capacity and order status. The AI agent guide documents requirements, implementation and testing.
